newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia Airlines buys six Airbus planes. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Croatia Airlines buys six Airbus planes. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: Croatia's national flag carrier Croatia Airlines said on Monday it signed an agreement to buy six medium-range A319 aircraft from the European manufacturer Airbus Industrie.
"Building of the first aircraft for Croatia Airlines...will begin immediately after the signing, for delivery in January 1998," the company said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
It ordered passenger type aircraft with 132 seats, of which 42 in the business class.
The deal, estimated at roughly $280 million, covers the purchase of six aircraft for delivery between year 1998 and 2000. It includes an option to buy another 10 planes by 2006.
Croatia Airlines will be able to opt in favour of larger A320 and A321 aircraft after it gets the first four planes, it said.
The deal also provides for the transfer of know-how for a future aircraft maintenance centre the company plans to build.

The agreement was signed in the presence of the Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa, visiting French minister Bernard Pons and French and German ambassadors to Zagreb, a government press officer said.
Croatia and France earlier on Monday reached an accord to boost mutual air traffic.

The government, which has a controlling stake in Croatia Airlines, hopes to offset a large portion of the purchase price with exports of Croatian goods, Assistant Transport Minister Zvonimir Vedris told Reuters.
"The firms that will be included are (aircraft engine supplier) Turbina from Karlovac and shipbuilders but we are also negotiating with some other companies," he said.
This is part of a larger purchase planned by the airline in a bid to swap out and expand its current nine-plane fleet.
Some of its aircraft are already 15 years old and have noisy engines which are unwelcome in the European Union countries which are its main destinations.
Airbus won the Croatian order worth up to $1.5 billion over the next 10 years in November 1996 against the other contender, American plane maker Boeing.
Although Croatia Airlines said at the time both suppliers had offered high technology and similar terms, by opting for Airbus it hoped to secure new business with the European Union.
Industry analysts believed Airbus put into the bargain a so-called "open-sky" offer which Boeing could not better.
Its planes were also said to have wider bodies, offering better comfort to passengers.
But the decision, made at very top of the Croatian government, was thought to have wider implications allowing the former Yugoslav republic to cement its shaky political ties with Europe.
